scope.base: staged changes across Portal 8d4cbf4, Agency 9b9f8a2, and Fabrikav2 12a1730e

intent: Add an authenticated Portal Agents workspace with exact-session steering and honest delivery receipts, formalize the studio game-release contract in Agency, and prepare a Find the Bird release candidate matching the Marble Run Portal shape.

findings.title: Producer HTML inherits terminal-steering authority
findings.suggested_fix: Serve kind=view content without ambient Portal authority, stop forwarding the global token, and give verdict submission only a request-scoped capability that cannot access Agents routes.
findings.why_it_matters: Scripted kind=view artifacts share the Portal origin and ambient cookie, so the new cookie-authenticated directory and message routes turn uploaded HTML into a principal that can steer live terminals.
evidence: portal/gallery/server.py:40 -- VIEW_HTML_CSP includes allow-scripts and allow-same-origin
portal/gallery/server.py:2331 -- Agents send accepts ambient web authentication
portal/gallery/server.py:2654 -- the global query token is forwarded into the media URL

findings.title: Replies can execute in a foreground shell
findings.suggested_fix: Immediately before input, verify the same provider PID/process group still owns the pane foreground TTY; fail before writing if identity changed, and report unknown if it changes between literal write and Enter.
findings.why_it_matters: An exited or suspended agent can leave a shell in the same pane, causing an authenticated Portal comment to execute as an operating-system command instead of reaching the agent approval boundary.
evidence: agency/src/agency/fleet/tmux.py:349 -- fresh target resolution verifies only the TTY-to-pane mapping
agency/src/agency/fleet/tmux.py:510 -- literal text is sent to the pane
agency/src/agency/fleet/tmux.py:521 -- Enter is sent separately

findings.title: Harness capture can falsely certify the production candidate
findings.suggested_fix: Label harness captures diagnostic-only and require a second install and capture from the exact harness-free production artifact, blocking publication when that lane is unavailable.
findings.first_evidence: agency/src/agency/catalog/skills/game/portal-game-release/SKILL.md:42 -- 4. **Gameplay evidence:** Load `game-device-verification` and use the canonical
findings.why_it_matters: The release skill requires evidence from the harness-free production candidate while the mandatory device skill builds a separate harness-enabled artifact, making the written contract contradictory or encouraging mismatched evidence.
evidence: agency/src/agency/catalog/skills/game/portal-game-release/SKILL.md:43 -- capture from the same candidate
game-device-verification/SKILL.md:38 -- build the harness-enabled native artifact

findings.title: Recover interrupted delivery claims
findings.suggested_fix: Reconcile persisted submitting records to unknown on startup with an append-only interrupted attempt so retry remains gated by explicit confirm_unknown.
findings.why_it_matters: A crash after the claim commit but before terminal completion leaves a message permanently submitting, with no retry path and no truthful recorded outcome.
evidence: portal/gallery/db.py:1136 -- the submitting claim commits before bridge invocation
portal/gallery/db.py:1120 -- retry allows pending and failed, plus explicitly confirmed unknown

findings.title: Lost HTTP response duplicates exact-session comments
findings.suggested_fix: Send a persistent client idempotency key, enforce uniqueness in Portal, return the existing delivery on repeats, and render transport failures as status unknown until history is reconciled.
findings.why_it_matters: If terminal submission succeeds but the response is lost, the form is re-enabled and a repeat creates a fresh message ID, bypassing unknown-state confirmation and duplicating agent input.
evidence: portal/gallery/server.py:2123 -- every initial request creates a new targeted message
portal/gallery/static/app.js:34 -- the unchanged form is enabled after transport failure

findings.title: Fallback SIDs leak local targets and vanish
findings.suggested_fix: Exclude path- or TTY-derived fallback SIDs until a genuine stable URL-safe provider SID exists, and enforce the same SID contract in directory and submit paths.
findings.why_it_matters: Fresh fallback IDs expose a local TTY or path and are then rejected by Portal, so the directory both leaks implementation detail and silently omits a live session.
evidence: agency/src/agency/fleet/state.py constructs codex and Claude fallback SIDs from local targets

findings.title: Duplicate SIDs are advertised but never submit
findings.suggested_fix: Build the reply directory in two passes and expose only provider-plus-SID pairs with exactly one eligible live row.
findings.why_it_matters: The UI offers controls for duplicate targets that submit_fleet_reply deterministically rejects as session_not_unique.
evidence: agency/src/agency/fleet/hud.py:103 -- submission requires exactly one provider-plus-SID match

findings.title: Bundle rewrite certifies missing and stale assets
findings.suggested_fix: Validate every required package asset against output existence, size, and SHA-256 before setting bundledInApp; resolve obsolete bw.png references and add missing/stale fixture tests.
findings.why_it_matters: The current candidate claims two levels are bundled while their package metadata references absent bw.png files and four copied assets disagree with recorded size/hash metadata.
evidence: generated dist and iOS bundles omit both referenced bw.png files
four of 36 manifested assets have stale sizes and hashes

findings.title: Validate Portal providers against Agency's enum
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict Portal to the explicit claude, codex, and pi capability set before persisting a targeted message.
findings.why_it_matters: Portal accepts targets Agency cannot parse, converting a certain preflight failure into a persisted ambiguous delivery.
evidence: agency/src/agency/cli.py uses FLEET_REPLY_PROVIDERS as argparse choices

findings.title: Unicode separators create permanently failed messages
findings.suggested_fix: Reject Unicode categories Cc, Zl, and Zp in Portal exactly as Agency does, with cross-contract boundary tests.
findings.first_evidence: portal/gallery/agents.py:40 -- return not any(ord(char) < 32 or ord(char) == 127 for char in value)
findings.why_it_matters: Portal persists characters Agency rejects, and retry resubmits the same invalid immutable text forever.
evidence: agency/src/agency/fleet/hud.py rejects Unicode Cc, Zl, and Zp categories

findings.title: Closing the internal stream permanently disables steering
findings.suggested_fix: Reserve agent-conversations from closure and recover any legacy closed instance before accepting new Agent messages.
findings.first_evidence: portal/gallery/server.py:2086 -- if stream is not None:
findings.why_it_matters: The supported close API can archive the one internal Agent stream, after which every future Agent message is rejected and no recovery path exists.
evidence: portal/gallery/db.py requires an open stream for targeted message creation

findings.title: Archived messages expose impossible retry actions
findings.suggested_fix: Carry the owning stream closed state into history and suppress failed and unknown retry controls for archived streams.
findings.why_it_matters: Archived history renders retry buttons that always return 409 because delivery claims require an open stream.
evidence: portal/gallery/templates/stream.html renders retry forms without checking stream.closed_at

findings.title: Add moved-pane tmux integration coverage
findings.suggested_fix: Add a disposable two-pane tmux integration that changes pane position, invokes exact provider-plus-SID delivery, and proves only the target receives the marker.
findings.first_evidence: agency/tests/test_fleet_tmux.py:233 -- with mock.patch.object(fmod, "_live_pane_id", return_value="%42") as live:
findings.why_it_matters: Mocked pane discovery and transport cannot prove the core safety property that a moved target does not redirect a comment to its neighbor.
evidence: No staged test starts disposable tmux panes or captures their real output

findings.title: Exercise bridge-exception delivery state
findings.suggested_fix: Make submit_to_agent raise in a route test and assert a durable unknown attempt plus confirmation-gated retry.
findings.first_evidence: portal/gallery/server.py:2110 -- except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 - an invoked bridge may already have submitted input
findings.why_it_matters: Without exercising the ambiguous exception path, a regression could produce a 500 or unsafe automatic retry after terminal input may already have been submitted.
evidence: staged tests cover a returned unknown outcome but never a raised bridge exception

triage_groups.title: Terminal authority and exactly-once steering
triage_groups.context: Untrusted content, pane identity, and transport ambiguity all sit on the operator-to-terminal authority boundary.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Isolate view authority first, bind delivery to the live foreground agent second, then add idempotent initial submission.
triage_groups.why: These fixes prevent comments from becoming shell commands or duplicate side effects.

triage_groups.title: Honest delivery recovery
triage_groups.context: Crash recovery and archived system-stream behavior must agree with the visible state machine.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Recover interrupted claims, reserve the system stream, suppress impossible controls, and pin the exception branch with a test.
triage_groups.why: Every badge and retry control must correspond to a legal durable transition.

triage_groups.title: Portal-Agency target contract
triage_groups.context: The directory, Portal preflight, and Agency mutation path currently accept different target and text domains.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Define one safe provider/SID/text contract and apply it at both serialization and submission boundaries.
triage_groups.why: A target advertised as replyable must be submit-able without leaking local machine identifiers.

triage_groups.title: Release candidate provenance
triage_groups.context: The workflow and bundle metadata can currently certify evidence or assets that do not belong to the claimed production candidate.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Separate diagnostic harness evidence from release evidence, then validate packaged asset bytes before setting bundle authority.
triage_groups.why: Portal should publish one coherent candidate, not an attractive collage of adjacent builds.

learnings: Portal browser tests are proxies; authenticated Agents flows still require inspected desktop and phone evidence.
Release checklists preserve evidence gates but do not themselves prove candidate coherence.
Packaged manifest authority must be checked against the actual native output, not only source fixtures.
deployment_notes: Find the Bird has a local signed candidate and browser proof, but matching physical-device gameplay is blocked by the offline iPhone and no Portal record was created.
Portal and Agency changes are isolated local worktree changes; no production deployment, Agency global sync, merge, or push occurred.
residual_risks: Terminal submission is not agent acknowledgement; the state model must continue to name that boundary honestly.
A provider-owned IPC transport would remove the remaining pane/process race more completely than tmux foreground checks.
Public game bundles still rely on a human secret/content inspection gate.
Manifest initialization has no concurrent-startup coverage.
Large targeted-message histories have no query-plan or latency measurement.
testing_gaps: Run inspected authenticated Agents flows at desktop and phone widths, including failed and confirmed-unknown states.
Run the exact physical production candidate on a named device before Find the Bird publication.
Measure unusually large targeted-message history only if Portal usage grows beyond its current single-user scale.

coverage.scope: owned staged changes across three isolated worktrees; untracked UX report and generated release files excluded
validator_false_reasons: Whitespace-only input was already rejected by the shared bounded-text helper before persistence.
failed_reviewers: adversarial peer-model pass returned non-parseable output and was non-blocking
